title: Ascending Neurons 2023 split-GAL4 lines
abstract:
This data set consists of central nervous system fluorescence images of Drosophila melanogaster driver lines and their genotypes. It includes raw confocal image data in Zeiss LSM format, along with H5J-compressed alignments to JRC2018, movies, maximum intensity projections (MIPs), and color-depth-encoded maximum intensity projections (CDMs).
Split-GAL4 AD and DBD combinations were designed by RM & BD and screened in initial split combinations crossed by Janelia's Fly Facility, and dissected, antibody labeled, and imaged by FlyLight. Images were scored by RM and successful AD/DBD combinations were made into stable lines by the Fly Facility and imaged again by FlyLight. Full genotypes are listed for each line.
These split-GAL4 lines were used in support of https://doi.org/10.1038/s41593-023-01281-z . In association with that work, other processed and aligned FlyLight images were made available at https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/S8AMKU .

narrative:
Short impact summary

This 2023 Drosophila neuroanatomy dataset shows early but meaningful scholarly uptake: it has 5 OpenAlex citations and 6 documented downstream reuses. The record also shows limited direct usage to date, with 2 views and no downloads captured in DataCite, suggesting an emerging resource that is being incorporated into related split-GAL4 work rather than broadly accessed through the repository.

Full narrative

“Ascending Neurons 2023 split-GAL4 lines” is a Figshare dataset centered on central nervous system fluorescence images and associated derived files for Drosophila melanogaster driver lines. The dataset includes raw confocal image data together with aligned outputs, movies, maximum intensity projections, and color-depth-encoded projections, supporting reuse in image-based neurobiology and driver-line characterization.

Its impact is concentrated in a small but clearly identifiable reuse network. OpenAlex records 5 citations, with citations appearing in 2024 and 2025, and the downstream works are closely aligned with the same research program on split-GAL4 driver line resources. The cited works are dominated by eLife and bioRxiv outputs, indicating that the dataset is being used in active, fast-moving neurogenetics research rather than only in slower-moving archival contexts.

Reuse evidence is stronger than the usage metrics might initially suggest. DataCite records 6 downstream reuses, including a linked associated article and multiple preprints and articles, which points to the dataset serving as an enabling resource for subsequent publications. This pattern is consistent with a methods- and resource-oriented dataset whose value is realized through incorporation into follow-on driver-line studies.

At the same time, the public record remains relatively sparse outside citation and reuse. DataCite shows only 2 views and no downloads, and there are no recorded event-data mentions in the available archive. In other words, the dataset’s demonstrated influence is still early and specialized: it is already embedded in a developing literature on Drosophila neuron types, but broader attention and general usage have not yet accumulated in the available sources.
